memory_update.text: SYY should remain the reference anchor for franchise supply-chain orchestration because public customer announcements explicitly frame Sysco as an enabler of national franchise expansion, quality control, ordering infrastructure, and standardized fulfillment.

PFGC is a plausible underfollowed public mapping for the node due to foodservice, specialty, convenience, and national chain distribution exposure; later layers should verify chain/franchise contract wins and margin sensitivity.

CHEF is an adjacent specialty-distribution candidate for restaurant procurement complexity, but the franchise/QSR exposure is not yet proven and should remain an inference until customer/channel mix is verified.
Private/co-op examples such as National DCP validate the node, but public-market mapping requires separating infrastructure providers from dependent customer stories like REBN.

node: Franchise procurement, sourcing, and supply-chain orchestration
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-market universe around outsourced restaurant and franchise supply-chain orchestration. The obvious anchor is Sysco, which validates the node because franchise and emerging restaurant systems use national foodservice distribution to standardize purchasing, fulfillment, quality control, and unit expansion. The underfollowed lane is more interesting: Performance Food Group and The Chefs' Warehouse offer less-mega-cap exposure to distribution density, specialty products, chain/restaurant customers, and procurement/logistics complexity. Reborn Coffee is included only as a speculative shadow/customer-dependency example because its 2026 Sysco partnership directly shows how a tiny franchisor may rely on an outsourced distribution platform for franchise readiness.
